1_executive_summary: P-22 — Multi-segment shape-memory polymer catheter with autonomous navigation toward op. A computationally specified P-22 concept plus a preregistered decisive experiment — not a validated technology. Current evidence: T1. Transfer posture: DECISIVE_EXPERIMENT_REQUIRED. Recommended transaction: RESEARCH_PARTNERSHIP (4 control problems). Validation cost: $20-50K.
2_industry_problem: Buckling: catheter WILL buckle before reaching actuation force limit (82x exceedance)

3_current_alternative.strongest_alternative: Intraoperative placement (surgeon-dependent). Published steerable catheters use closed-loop control + sensing + passive safety (PubMed 25684857).
3_current_alternative.alternative_weakness: Manual placement depends on surgeon skill
3_current_alternative.why_inadequate: Can a buckling-safe architecture with closed-loop control navigate safely without tissue damage?

4_technology_advantage_hypothesis.differentiation: Differentiation hypothesis: Can a buckling-safe architecture with closed-loop control navigate safely without tissue damage?
evidence_against: Buckling: catheter WILL buckle before reaching actuation force limit (82x exceedance)
Control stability NOT modeled (30s delay makes PID unstable)
Tissue safety: effective force 0.039 N exceeds estimated damage threshold 0.01 N by 4x
4_technology_advantage_hypothesis.unresolved_question: Can a buckling-safe architecture with closed-loop control navigate safely without tissue damage?
